accepted.reason: Best aligns with hospitalization semantics (admissions lag infections) while keeping dynamics simple/identifiable for a short single-season series (31 train weeks). delayed_I is explicitly recommended and avoids adding a potentially weakly identifiable H compartment.

Also well-aligned with hospitalization semantics and directly probes whether a shorter, plausible 1-week lag explains the data without invoking fractional memory. Low added complexity and helps assess delay identifiability given moderate peakiness.

Useful as a no-lag comparator to test whether the observed hospitalization-rate behaves nearly contemporaneously with an infection proxy in this age group. Still simple and identifiable, though less semantically plausible than delayed_I with lag >0.

Reasonable robustness check for longer lag without changing structure type. Still identifiable (single extra discrete lag choice) and consistent with delayed_I being more plausible than an explicit H compartment for short series, though 3 weeks risks misalignment.

rejected.reason: Fractional memory is not clearly justified by the series summary (single season, moderate peakiness, 31 training points) and adds flexibility that increases overfitting/identifiability risk. Given prior patterns already included a fractional delayed_I variant, this proposal is more likely to repeat instability than to provide interpretable gains.

suggested_edits.edit: Clarify that delay=3 is a sensitivity/robustness probe rather than a primary mechanistic assumption, and note that with only 31 training weeks the lag may be weakly identifiable; interpret any apparent improvement cautiously as potential phase-shift fitting rather than true process lag.

Frame delay=0 explicitly as a diagnostic baseline for phase alignment (not a mechanistic hospitalization model), and pre-specify that if it fits similarly to delayed_I, the delay parameter may be poorly identifiable in this series.
